thread:
maria g: Quick question — we added TTL for ephemeral embeddings (30d) in the vector-store. If the EKM rotates keys, what happens to delete propagation for DSARs? do we need to rewrap before deletions?
samir p: Short answer: rotation shouldn't block logical deletes, but it can break access to raw ciphertext if we rely on rewrap-only paths. depends on whether deletion job needs to decrypt for matching.
kai l: Context: our delete pipeline does two steps: 1) find candidate vectors via id/tags, 2) remove objects from object-store and drop index entries. We don't decrypt during matching — we use metadata + deterministic ids. so EKM rotate ~should be safe.
maria g: Good to know. But we saw one edgecase: an old backup snapshot had embedded blobs encrypted with a retired key and the retention job failed to remove them because the backup service attempted a verify/decrypt step.
ashley: That explains the retention exception ticket earlier. Backup service still tries to validate integrity (decrypt) before tombstoning. If key is retired, the attempt fails and the job aborts.
sec-bot: Incident #INC-2026-089 created: "backup-delete-failure-on-retired-key" — assigned to ashley, priority P2.
olivia r: Proposal: change backup purge path to mark objects as "pending-delete" without decrypting; add a subsequent reconciliation worker that uses key-rewrap/privileged-unwrap to scrub ciphertext when keys are available. That avoids blocking DSAR deletes.
samir p: +1 but we need RBAC guardrails. Only a narrow service identity can perform unwrap/re-encrypt. Add audit event for both mark and final scrub.
kai l: Also add an entry in audit-indexing so DSAR owners can query every deletion: fields = [object_id, dsar_id, performed_by, key_id_at_delete, method]. We can emit a structured log line like:
```
{"evt":"dsar_delete","obj":"vec-...","dsar":"DSAR-1234","by":"backup-svc","key":"ekm:v2","method":"mark-only"}
```
maria g: For immediate workaround, can we run a one-off migration that rewraps retired-key blobs to current key using breakglass? what's the risk?
ashley: Breakglass rewrap will work, but needs KMS ops quota and manual audit. Legal asked for a retention-exception record before we touch subject data.
olivia r: If legal requires retention exception, we should document: reason, scope (snapshots: 2024-10-01..2025-01-01), approved by legal@, TTL override flag. Keep that metadata in the DSAR ticket.
samir p: Action items:
- [samir] add audit events for mark & scrub (eta 2d)
- [kai] update backup purge to mark w/o decrypt (eta 3d)
- [ashley] run controlled rewrap for affected snapshots after legal signoff (coord with sec & legal)
- [maria] update DSAR runbook note about EKM rotation edgecases (eta 1d)

maria g: Thanks — tagging legal: @olivia r for the retention-exception checklist and signoff process :pray:
olivia r: Got it, I'll draft the retention exception template and link to INC-2026-089. Also we'll require X-Request-ID in delete API calls for traceability.
samir p: Example delete call for ops reference:
```
curl -X POST https://internal-api/delete -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Request-ID: dsar-1234" -d '{"object_ids": ["vec-abc"], "reason":"DSAR-delete"}'
```
maria g: Perfect. I'll add that to the runbook and close the loop once audit events land.
